author: Danny Garrison
title: Post-Week 6 Power Rankings
body:
## 1. Whit (Nightmare at the Substation) | —
Result: W vs. Ryan
Record: 6-0
Week 6 Points: 105.24
Top Scorer: Trevor Lawrence, 28.34

Whit is the second-highest scoring team and has faced the least points against so far. What a stress-free way to live.

## 2. Dave (That's Rice) | —
Result: W vs. Nick
Record: 5-1
Week 6 Points: 101.00
Top Scorer: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Matthew Golden, 19.40

Derrick Henry Washed Watch starts now.

## 3. Corey (Endzone Chef) | ▲ 1
Result: W vs. Mike
Record: 4-2
Week 6 Points: 112.10
Top Scorer: James Cook III, 22.80

With Davante Adams gone and Josh Jacobs back, Corey finds himself in a severe RB/WR imbalance.

## 4. Steve (Maye I Get Off This Achane?) | ▲ 2
Result: W vs. Danny
Record: 4-2
Week 6 Points: 126.20
Top Scorer: Drake Maye, 23.80

Steve was a decent DST performance away from Week 6's top score but either way he's cruising after a shaky start. Drake Maye and Colston Loveland starting to resemble what we thought they'd be is bad news for the rest of us.

## 5. Danny (Motion Party) | —
Result: L vs. Steve
Record: 3-3
Week 6 Points: 108.66
Top Scorer: Tyler Shough, 26.96

I want to personally apologize to Kenneth Walker for involving him in so many losses because he's a fucking winner.

## 6. Nick (Easy Pickens) | ▼ 3
Result: L vs. Dave
Record: 3-3
Week 6 Points: 86.60
Top Scorer: Jonathan Taylor, 20.10

Disastrous week for Nick, who lost Terry McLaurin for the year, possibly Mike Evans for weeks, and Cam Skattebo until John Harbaugh decides he's learned his lesson (Cam Skattebo will never learn his lesson).

## 7. Beau (IM SORRY HUE JACKSON) | —
Result: W vs. Andrew
Record: 3-3
Week 6 Points: 91.14
Top Scorer: Jordan Love, 21.24

Beau squeaked by with a low-scoring win while his Bengals stack was on a bye. These are the weeks that decide seasons.

## 8. Craig (Chat ADP) | ▲ 4
Result: W vs. Evan
Record: 2-4
Week 6 Points: 130.12
Top Scorer: Christian McCaffrey, 26.20

Craig saw another sacko flashing before his eyes and found another gear.

## 9. Andrew (Mayor of TD City) | ▼ 1
Result: L vs. Beau
Record: 2-4
Week 6 Points: 81.42
Top Scorer: Dak Prescott, 13.02

Disappointed by Dak Prescott's lack of production when he is surrounded by all the pieces he should need to succeed? Welcome to my life.

## 10. Evan (11 Humans vs. 1 Robot) | ▼ 1
Result: L vs. Craig
Record: 1-5
Week 6 Points: 69.78
Top Scorer: Chiefs Defense, 15.00

Evan is in hell. After starting the season with a run of bad breaks, he faced off against Craig's team in what should've been a get-right game. Then Evan promptly turned in his worst performance of the year and Craig blew him out. Evan's total points lead should give him cushion in a tiebreaker down the line but not if he's done winning games for the year.

## 11. Ryan (Uncle Jeff's Prodigy) | ▼ 1
Result: L vs. Whit
Record: 2-4
Week 6 Points: 67.98
Top Scorer: Matthew Stafford, 16.88

Lowest-scoring team in the league. A.J. Brown is back and can't catch. Saquon Barkley's team is now tanking. Matt Stafford is 100 years old and looks like it. What will it take for Ryan to just do his punishment and lift the curse? Maybe another punishment.

## 12. Mike (Chasing 500 (Again)) | ▼ 1
Result: L vs. Corey
Record: 1-5
Week 6 Points: 77.36
Top Scorer: Brock Purdy, 17.36

Justin Jefferson has his work cut out for him if he's going to save Mike from a sacko.

author: Danny Garrison
title: Post-Week 5 Power Rankings
body:
## 1. Whit (Nightmare at the Substation) | —
Result: W vs. Craig
Record: 5-0
Week 5 Points: 137.82
Top Scorer: Jahmyr Gibbs, 35.20

Starting to get concerned about Whit pulling off an undefeated season and putting the FOL history books even further out of reach for the rest of us.

## 2. Dave (That's Rice) | —
Result: W vs. Corey
Record: 4-1
Week 5 Points: 165.78
Top Scorer: Jaylen Warren, 33.80

Dave heard the rumblings all last week. "Is Dave a fraud?" "Is That's Rice🎙️🎶 finished??" And turned that into bulletin board material for Jaylen Warren. He nearly doubled his Week 4 points in Week 5 and he's got a stranglehold on the total points tiebreaker if Whit ever loses a game.

## 3. Nick (Easy Pickens) | ▲ 2
Result: W vs. Ryan
Record: 3-2
Week 5 Points: 113.70
Top Scorer: Josh Allen, 31.50

Josh Allen once again did Josh Allen things.

## 4. Corey (Endzone Chef) | —
Result: L vs. Dave
Record: 3-2
Week 5 Points: 128.16
Top Scorer: Jayden Daniels, 32.26

Corey's team is doing just fine with zero bench depth, so I guess he will continue to hold his Josh Jacobs and Tyreek Hill stashes. But two more injuries on top of DeVonta Smith's absence make it a very dicey proposition.

## 5. Danny (Motion Party) | ▲ 1
Result: W vs. Beau
Record: 3-2
Week 5 Points: 151.34
Top Scorer: Puka Nacua, 29.20

Thinking I could trust the Cowboys defense, even against an undrafted rookie QB making his second career start on a short week, is my own fault. There is no floor to how embarrassing that unit can be, and I should've known that. Good thing the rest of Motion Party is resurgent.

## 6. Steve (Maye I Get Off This Achane?) | ▼ 3
Result: L vs. Mike
Record: 3-2
Week 5 Points: 83.46
Top Scorer: Drake Maye, 39.46

Drake Maye tried to prop up Steve's entire team last week but even a 40-burger from his QB couldn't paper over the wasteland down the rest of his lineup.

## 7. Beau (IM SORRY HUE JACKSON) | —
Result: L vs. Danny
Record: 2-3
Week 5 Points: 134.40
Top Scorer: Joe Burrow, 24.60

It always hurts to put up a big score in a loss but Beau will be glad to have all those points when we're sorting out the logjam of .500 teams at the end of the regular season.

## 8. Andrew (Mayor of TD City) | ▲ 3
Result: W vs. Evan
Record: 2-3
Week 5 Points: 127.24
Top Scorer: Christian Watson, 29.30

Andrew's once-promising running back situation continues to be an unmitigated disaster but he emphatically stopped his nosedive last week thanks to Christian Watson, who might be the best WR in the league.

## 9. Evan (11 Humans vs. 1 Robot) | —
Result: L vs. Andrew
Record: 1-4
Week 5 Points: 122.54
Top Scorer: Jameis Winston, 25.74

My heart goes out to Evan. Hasn't scored less than 100 in any week, yet he's 1-4 with 4-straight losses. 5th highest-scoring team and tied for last in the standings. His team is good enough to turn it around but might be too little too late.

## 10. Ryan (Uncle Jeff's Prodigy) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Nick
Record: 2-3
Week 5 Points: 85.52
Top Scorer: Matthew Stafford, 27.32

Still cursed.

## 11. Mike (Chasing 500 (Again)) | ▲ 1
Result: W vs. Steve
Record: 1-4
Week 5 Points: 96.16
Top Scorer: Bucky Irving, 30.50

Mike scratched and clawed his way to his first win of the season to make the battle for last place very interesting going forward.

## 12. Craig (Chat ADP) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Whit
Record: 1-4
Week 5 Points: 95.92
Top Scorer: Malik Nabers, 23.60

Just 0.24 points separated Craig and Mike in Week 5 and just 0.06 points separate them in the tiebreaker. We've got a dogfight for the sacko.

author: Danny Garrison
title: Post-Week 4 Power Rankings
body:
## 1. Whit (Nightmare at the Substation) | —
Result: W vs. Andrew
Record: 4-0
Week 4 Points: 118.98
Top Scorer: Kyren Williams, 31.70

While others loudly campaigned for the No. 1 spot, Whit continued to quietly and methodically win games behind the unstoppable force that is Jahmyr Gibbs. Now, he's the only remaining unbeaten.

## 2. Dave (That's Rice) | —
Result: L vs. Steve
Record: 3-1
Week 4 Points: 95.36
Top Scorer: Bryce Young, 21.46

Dave turned in his first sub-100 performance last week and paid for it with his first loss. He still probably has the strongest top-to-bottom roster in the league though, and he's still the highest scorer by a slim margin.

## 3. Steve (Maye I Get Off This Achane?) | ▲ 2
Result: W vs. Dave
Record: 3-1
Week 4 Points: 121.64
Top Scorer: CeeDee Lamb, 32.80

Steve is on a mission. He's won three straight and he's hot on Dave's heels, tied at 3-1 and trailing by a mere 142.86 in the total points tiebreaker.

## 4. Corey (Endzone Chef) | —
Result: W vs. Ryan
Record: 3-1
Week 4 Points: 96.62
Top Scorer: Chuba Hubbard, 25.40

Obviously the week someone actually put Kalif Raymond in their starting lineup he was going to turn into a pumpkin.

## 5. Nick (Easy Pickens) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Craig
Record: 2-2
Week 4 Points: 108.82
Top Scorer: Jonathan Taylor, 22.20

You're not gonna believe this, but Cam Skattebo is questionable with a new injury.

## 6. Danny (Motion Party) | ▲ 4
Result: W vs. Mike
Record: 2-2
Week 4 Points: 144.18
Top Scorer: Kenneth Walker III, 30.40

With all Chargers purged from the starting lineup, Motion Party was finally and joyously free. Puka is back, K9 never left, and I have gobbled up all the waiver wire running backs. What can possibly go wrong now?

## 7. Beau (IM SORRY HUE JACKSON) | ▲ 1
Result: W vs. Evan
Record: 2-2
Week 4 Points: 118.82
Top Scorer: Javonte Williams, 28.80

Beau survived the Ja'Marr Chase concussion game, but if Chase misses this week Beau faces the gruesome prospect of choosing between DK Metcalf and Jordan Addison for his starting lineup.

## 8. Ryan (Uncle Jeff's Prodigy) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Corey
Record: 2-2
Week 4 Points: 87.72
Top Scorer: Tee Higgins, 21.20

Things are getting dark for Ryan, as the curse of being delinquent on his punishment continues to take its toll. This week he could be without all of his top-4 picks with Saquon Barkley, A.J. Brown, Breece Hall, and Tee Higgins all very injured.

## 9. Evan (11 Humans vs. 1 Robot) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Beau
Record: 1-3
Week 4 Points: 103.70
Top Scorer: Bijan Robinson, 27.20

Evan admirably duct-taped over his running back problem with 20 points from Alvin Kamara falling into the endzone. But too many duds on the rest of his roster dropped him to a harsh 1-3 record despite being the 4th highest scoring team in the league thus far.

## 10. Craig (Chat ADP) | ▲ 2
Result: W vs. Nick
Record: 1-3
Week 4 Points: 139.98
Top Scorer: Tetairoa McMillan, 38.20

Just days after I called him out for failing to ever break 90, Craig almost snatched the high-scorer payout from me in Week 4.

## 11. Andrew (Mayor of TD City) | ▼ 2
Result: L vs. Whit
Record: 1-3
Week 4 Points: 68.50
Top Scorer: Dak Prescott, 18.10

Andrew's nosedive has been astounding. His score has fallen by double digits every week so far, going from 143.16 in Week 1 to 68.50 in Week 4. One would imagine he has to have found the floor now.

## 12. Mike (Chasing 500 (Again)) | ▼ 1
Result: L vs. Danny
Record: 0-4
Week 4 Points: 80.82
Top Scorer: Zay Flowers, 21.80

Mike carrying an empty bench spot in our extremely limited-bench-spot league was an interesting intimidation tactic that didn't entirely pan out.

author: Danny Garrison
title: 2026 Post-Draft Power Rankings
body:
Welcome back, league.

A lot has changed since the very first draft 10 years ago. We've had weddings, births, moves, Amazon defections, and many other major life changes as time has marched on. But it's nice to know some things stay the same, like the little circular arrows over Craig's profile picture that indicate he's on autodraft or the first Brown coming off the board way too early.

As always, Yahoo's draft grades are offensively bad. AI can build us a stunning website, but you know what it can't do? Know ball.

That's what you have me for.

## 1. Whit | 2025: 10-4, runner-up
The two trendiest WRs of the offseason paired with three potential RB1s. But unfortunately any roster with BTJ on it is cursed.
[roster]
QB: Trevor Lawrence
RB: Jahmyr Gibbs, Kyren Williams, Ashton Jeanty, Jordan Mason
WR: Emeka Egbuka, Luther Burden III, Brian Thomas Jr., Michael Wilson
TE: Travis Kelce, Isaiah Likely
[/roster]

## 2. Beau | 2025: 9-5, made playoffs
The deadliest stack in modern fantasy history. And it's an even year, so the Bengals might even be relevant past November.
[roster]
QB: Joe Burrow
RB: Javonte Williams, Quinshon Judkins, Aaron Jones Sr., Tyler Allgeier
WR: Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London, DK Metcalf, Jordan Addison, Xavier Worthy
TE: Tyler Warren
[/roster]

## 3. Danny | 2025: 7-7, missed playoffs
With Mike McDaniel on the sticks, Justin Herbert could become Tom Brady on even more steroids. If Mike chooses to funnel targets to Ladd and doesn't do something stupid like run the ball, this stack could go ballistic.
[roster]
QB: Justin Herbert
RB: Kenneth Walker III, Travis Etienne Jr., Kenny Gainwell, Emmett Johnson
WR: Puka Nacua, Ladd McConkey, Jameson Williams, Parker Washington, KC Concepcion
TE: Kyle Pitts Sr.
[/roster]

## 4. Steve | 2025: 5-9, missed playoffs
High floors, high ceilings, and depth. And De'Von Achane might touch the ball 50 times per game since the Dolphins' other starters are plumbers and insurance salesmen.
[roster]
QB: Drake Maye
RB: De'Von Achane, Bhayshul Tuten, Rico Dowdle, RJ Harvey, Kyle Monangai
WR: CeeDee Lamb, Jaylen Waddle, Quentin Johnston, Wan'Dale Robinson
TE: Colston Loveland
[/roster]

## 5. Ryan | 2025: 2-12, last place
I would normally advise against a QB/RB/TE pairing from the same team but Ryan might have every Eagles TD for the entire season on his roster.
[roster]
QB: Jalen Hurts
RB: Saquon Barkley, Breece Hall, David Montgomery
WR: A.J. Brown, Tee Higgins, Stefon Diggs, Michael Pittman Jr., Jakobi Meyers
TE: Sam LaPorta, Dallas Goedert
[/roster]

## 6. Craig | 2025: 6-8, missed playoffs
Autodraft might have cooked here. I don't know if I've ever seen that many questionable tags in a Week 1 lineup but the upside is big.
[roster]
QB: Lamar Jackson, Dak Prescott
RB: Christian McCaffrey, Jonathon Brooks, Rachaad White
WR: Nico Collins, Malik Nabers, Tetairoa McMillan, Chris Godwin Jr., Romeo Doubs
TE: Tucker Kraft
[/roster]

## 7. Andrew | 2025: 9-5, champion
There's a lot of depth on this roster but injuries could quickly derail Andrew's quest for a repeat.
[roster]
QB: Jayden Daniels
RB: Omarion Hampton, Jeremiyah Love, D'Andre Swift, Jadarian Price
WR: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Christian Watson, Josh Downs, Makai Lemon, Jalen Coker
TE: Mark Andrews
[/roster]

## 8. Dave | 2025: 9-5, made playoffs
Eventually someone will get caught holding the bag when Derrick Henry falls off, but I don't think this is the year.
[roster]
QB: Caleb Williams
RB: Derrick Henry, Rhamondre Stevenson, Jaylen Warren, Chris Rodriguez Jr., Zach Charbonnet
WR: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashee Rice, De'Zhaun Stribling, Matthew Golden
TE: Trey McBride
[/roster]

## 9. Nick | 2025: 8-6, made playoffs
Two of Nick's top four picks are at risk of having a mental health crisis that keeps them off the field but he also has Josh Allen so he has hope.
[roster]
QB: Josh Allen
RB: Jonathan Taylor, Cam Skattebo, Tony Pollard, Jacory Croskey-Merritt
WR: George Pickens, Terry McLaurin, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., Jordyn Tyson
TE: George Kittle
[/roster]

## 10. Evan | 2025: 5-9, missed playoffs
It turns out there is one Kyler Murray believer left.
[roster]
